idiom_name: hand-written joined queries over per-class tables (GRDB / SQLite)
implementation_notes: Swift has class inheritance and the platform frameworks model it - but Core Data/SwiftData store every entity of a hierarchy in one table, which is single table inheritance rather than this pattern, so one table per class means dropping to SQL with GRDB (or mapping onto an existing per-class schema). What replaces the classic mapper is a record type per table plus a fetch that joins base and subtype tables and builds the right subclass from the type code. The joined form is justified when the schema already has one table per class, when subtype columns must be NOT NULL, or when the data lives in a shared SQLite database.
code_sketch:
struct Person: FetchableRecord, Decodable {
    var id: Int64
    var name: String
    var birthDate: String      // person table column
}
let sql = """
SELECT p.id, p.name, e.birth_date
  FROM party p JOIN person e ON e.id = p.id
 WHERE p.id = ?
"""
let person = try Person.fetchOne(db, sql: sql, arguments: [id])
pitfalls: The platform frameworks cannot express this layout, so choosing it per hierarchy is a one-way door: Core Data/SwiftData migrations and predicates stop applying to that part of the model.
SQLite enforces foreign keys only with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON, so the PK/FK invariant the pattern relies on must be enabled at open time or it silently does not exist.
